caption: “Gaultheria procumbens.” Partridge Berry (Figure 1) with "The bractes or outer calyx" (Figure 2), "The true calyx" (Figure 3), "Stamen of the natural size" (Figure 4), "Anther magnified, the dark places showing the mode of opening” (Figure 5), "Calyx and pistil" (Figure 6), "Fruit" (Figure 7), "Longitudinal section of the fruit" (Figure 8), and the "Transverse section of the capsule" (Figure 9). Plate XXII from Jacob Bigelow. American Medical Botany, Being a Collection of the Native Medicinal Plants of the United States. Vol. 2. Boston: Cummings and Hilliard, 1818.
alt: A coloured engraving on toned paper, Plate XXII: two leafy stems of wintergreen with broad green leaves and small white bell flowers, rising from a creeping root, above a row of nine small numbered drawings of the flower's and fruit's parts, with “Gaultheria procumbens” in script below.
title: Gaultheria procumbens
